items.title: Generally Available: Higher limit of Azure Blob Storage accounts per region per subscription
items.description:
Higher Azure Storage account resource quotas are now generally available, supporting up to 1,000 storage accounts with standard endpoints per region, per subscription, up from the default of 250. Manage more accounts in a single subscription, reducing the need to distribute resources across multiple subscriptions. 

Request quota increases through the Azure Portal, Azure CLI, or Azure PowerShell without opening a support ticket. Azure Storage Resource Provider (SRP) API read, write, and list operations automatically scale to support higher approved account quotas. 

These changes apply to account management operations through the Storage Resource Provider control plane, not to data plane operations within a storage account.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Cost management and tagging for Claude models in Microsoft Foundry
items.description:
Microsoft Foundry now brings Claude models into Azure Cost Management alongside the rest of your Foundry spend, generally available. Until now, Claude charges appeared under SaaS rather than under the Foundry resource used to deploy them, and Claude deployments lacked the tags enterprises rely on for showback and chargeback, leaving finance and platform teams to reconcile costs by hand. With this release, Claude costs appear under the associated Foundry resource; Claude deployments and Foundry resources support tags that follow your organization's existing conventions; and Claude cost records carry model and usage_type tags, so you can filter and group spending by Claude model and separate input-token from output-token costs. Customers get one consistent, resource-level view of Claude spending and can allocate usage to the responsible teams and workloads without a separate reconciliation process. To get started, open Cost analysis in Azure Cost Management and group by resource or tag. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Front Door profile and route level WAF policies
items.description:
Announcing the general availability of profile and route level policies for Azure Web Application Firewall (WAF) on Azure Front Door Premium. WAF policies are no longer limited to individual domains: you can now apply broad baseline protection across an entire Azure Front Door profile and use targeted policies for the routes that need different controls.   

You can associate a WAF policy at the profile, domain, or route scope. For example, use a profile level policy for common protections across every domain in a profile, then apply a route level policy to sensitive paths such as sign-in, checkout, or API routes. This reduces policy duplication for teams that run many applications behind a single Azure Front Door profile, while keeping granular controls where they're needed.   

When more than one scope applies to a request, Azure Front Door uses the most specific policy: a route level policy takes precedence over a domain level policy, and a domain level policy takes precedence over a profile level policy. Existing domain level associations continue to work without any changes.   

Learn more.
